subject: Realtime streaming plateau: prolonged silence during burst tests — exec attention requested
messages:
From: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@novanet.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: coretech-support@novanet.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:15:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Realtime feed — intermittent silence during high-throughput bursts

Hi Jasmine,

We hit a production issue starting ~08:05 PST this morning during a scheduled high-throughput replay. Rough summary: about 30% of active realtime sessions experienced a prolonged silence (no token/chunk output) for 5–30s followed by either a truncated response or a client-side WebSocket timeout.

Symptoms observed by our clients:
- WebSocket stays open, no chunks arrive for 6–20 seconds, then the connection either resumes or the client reports a 504/timeout.
- p95 response latency jumped to ~2.3s (baseline ~120ms) during the window.
- Error rate around 3.8% (502/timeout) across affected endpoints.

We attached a HAR and some server-side logs for the replay window (novanet-replay-20261111.har, novanet-logs-20261111.tar.gz). This is affecting a live cohort — roughly 60% of sessions in the replay traffic slice. We need immediate help; can you confirm whether this looks like chunk coalescing / proxy buffering or something on your inference runtime?

Thanks,
Evan Shaw
CTO, Novanet

Attachment: novanet-replay-20261111.har (HAR trace)
Attachment: novanet-logs-20261111.tar.gz (server logs)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@novanet.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:28:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Realtime feed — intermittent silence during high-throughput bursts

Evan — thanks for the quick report and attachments. We’ve opened an internal incident (JIRA-STREAM-5421) and I’m looping in SRE (Marissa), runtime (David) and the on-call for streaming infra (Soojin).

Immediate asks:
- Can you point us to a single example trace id from the HAR (request id / ws session id) so we can correlate?
- Did this coincide with any model rollout or routing change on your side?
- Did you see the same behavior for our fallback route (route-fallback-us-west)?

Short-term mitigation we can try while we triage:
- Route a subset of traffic to a dedicated node pool for Novanet (isolated capacity) — I can coordinate with infra if you approve.
- Disable chunk coalescing on the proxy (we can flip a flag) or increase WS keepalive frequency.

I’ll update in ~15–30 min with what we find. Attaching brief diagnostic checklist for the replay to nail down the repro.

— Jasmine
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: diagnostic-guidance.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:42:11 -0800
Subject: Re: Realtime feed — intermittent silence during high-throughput bursts

On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 08:28 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Evan — thanks for the quick report...

Triage notes from an initial pass on the cluster serving Novanet:
- Observed a correlated spike in concurrent in-flight requests at 08:04–08:10 PST. Token emission rate dipped; KV-cache eviction count rose 3.6x which maps to increased cache misses.
- Proxy (edge) metrics show an increase in buffered writes and a small but sustained backlog in the connection writer thread. This aligns with chunk coalescing getting delayed under bursty load.
- Keepalive pings from the WS proxy were delayed; in several sessions the last ping was logged but the chunk stream had stopped emitting tokens.

Preliminary hypothesis: under sudden burst load we are seeing a combination of (a) runtime backpressure causing emission pauses, and (b) proxy coalescing/buffer thresholds delaying chunk flushes so clients experience a silence window.

Immediate recommended actions (safe, reversible):
1) Roll Novanet traffic to isolated dedicated nodes (no multi-tenant co-location) — reduces cross-tenant interference.
2) Disable proxy chunk coalescing (edge flag) and decrease coalescing window from 25ms -> 5ms.
3) Reduce max batching window in runtime for Novanet workload to avoid large batch stalls.
4) Temporarily increase WS keepalive frequency to 10s from 30s.

I’ll kick off changes 1 and 2 now in the canary pool and monitor. If we still see silence windows after that, we escalate to runtime team for deeper kernel / KV cache analysis.

— Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@novanet.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: coretech-support@novanet.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:59 -0800
Subject: Re: Realtime feed — intermittent silence during high-throughput bursts

Thanks Jasmine / Marissa — attaching the replay subset (novanet-logs-20261111.tar.gz) and one annotated screenshot showing the client-side timeline where chunks stop arriving (screenshot-heartbeat-fail.png).

Additional data points:
- This also showed up in EU-West during our simultaneous run there, so it’s not limited to a single region.
- Overall error spike ~4.2% across two regions during the window.
- We did not change routing or model versions on our side; the replay was a strict replay of production traffic.

We approve routing traffic to dedicated nodes for the immediate mitigation. We’re also happy to flip ancillary settings you recommend while you triage. This is impacting a paying customer cohort, so we’d like an exec sync if possible.

— Evan
Evan Shaw
CTO, Novanet

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@novanet.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:42:10 -0800
Subject: URGENT: exec sync requested — Novanet realtime silence during burst windows

Team — quick executive summary for leadership / product: Novanet reported significant realtime session silence during scheduled high-throughput replays on 2026-11-11 (incidents in US-West and EU-West). Impact: ~60% of replay sessions experienced at least one silence window; total error rate bump ~4% and p95 latency rose to ~2.3s. This is customer-impacting for a paid cohort (related account: Novanet, deal: DEAL-2986).

What we’ve done so far:
- Opened incident JIRA-STREAM-5421 and began triage (Marissa).
- Rolled Novanet traffic to an isolated canary dedicated pool and disabled proxy chunk coalescing in canary.
- Increased WS keepalive cadence in canary and reduced runtime batching window for the canary.

Observed result: early canary shows a 70% reduction in silence windows (prelim). We need a broader rollout plan if this persists.

Recommended next steps for exec approval:
1) Approve failover of Novanet to dedicated capacity for 24–48h (reduces multi-tenant coupling).
2) Offer a one-time service credit for the affected cohort and schedule a joint post-mortem with Novanet within 72h.
3) Prioritize a runtime change to make chunk flush behavior more resilient under KV-cache churn (medium priority P1).

I’m requesting an exec sync in the next 90 minutes to confirm the capacity move and credits. Evan — can you be available for a 30-min readout?

— Jasmine Liu
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
